questions.question: From which locations can a dispatcher dispatch work order tasks to qualified agents in Field Service Management?

options.text: Dispatch queue, task map, and Dispatcher Workspace
Work Order form, Agent Calendar, and Service Portal
Task map, Flow Designer, and Mobile Agent
Dispatcher Workspace, Agent Workspace, and Service Catalog

explanation.correct: Dispatchers can dispatch work order tasks from three locations: the Dispatch queue (dispatch tasks from task records), the Task map (dispatch using a Google map with geolocation), and Dispatcher Workspace (dispatch using drag-and-drop and auto-assign capabilities).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Agent Calendar and Service Portal are not dispatch locations. The Work Order form itself is not used for dispatching tasks.
Flow Designer is a workflow automation tool, not a dispatch location. Mobile Agent is used by field agents, not dispatchers for task assignment.
Agent Workspace and Service Catalog are not dispatch locations. Agent Workspace is for customer service agents, not field service dispatching.

source.excerpt: You can dispatch work order tasks to qualified work agents from these locations: Dispatch queue: Dispatch tasks to agents from task records. Task map: Dispatch tasks to agents using a Google map with geolocation. Dispatcher Workspace: Dispatch tasks to agents using the drag-and-drop and auto-assign capabilities.

questions.question: Which capabilities are available to field agents when using the Now Mobile Agent application in offline mode? (Choose two.)

options.text: Auto-dispatch tasks to other agents
Accept or reject assigned tasks
Create new part requirements
Modify work order templates
Reassign tasks to different crews

explanation.correct: When working offline with the Now Mobile Agent application, field agents can accept or reject tasks assigned to them and create new part requirements. These offline capabilities allow agents to continue productive work at task sites without internet connectivity.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Auto-dispatch is a dispatcher function performed from the dispatch queue or Dispatcher Workspace, not a mobile agent capability. Agents cannot dispatch tasks to other agents.
Work order templates are administrative configurations requiring wm_admin or model_manager roles, not field agent offline capabilities.
Task reassignment is a dispatcher function, not available to field agents. Agents work on tasks assigned to them but cannot reassign to others.

source.excerpt: Start working on tasks by accepting or rejecting tasks assigned to you... Create a part requirement. Create a new part requirement when offline: Request inventory

questions.question: Which fields can be configured in the Task Information section of a Work Order Template? (Choose three.)

options.text: Work Configuration
Agent Performance Metrics
Task Skills
Checklist Template
Customer Satisfaction Score
SLA Breach Notifications

explanation.correct: The Task Information section of a Work Order Template includes Work Configuration (which automatically populates Task type and Work type fields), Task Skills (skills required by an agent with mandatory indicators), and Checklist Template (to add checklists to tasks created from the template).

wrongAnswers.explanation: Agent Performance Metrics are reporting and analytics features, not configurable fields in work order templates.
Customer Satisfaction Score is a post-service measurement collected after work completion, not a template configuration field.
SLA Breach Notifications are configured through SLA definitions and workflows, not within work order template task information.

source.excerpt: Task information: Work configuration - The Work configuration for this task. Selecting a work configuration will automatically populate the Task type and Work type fields... Task skills - Skills required by an agent to work on the task... Checklist template - Select a checklist template to add a checklist to the tasks created from this work order template.

questions.question: Which role is NOT authorized to dispatch work order tasks in Field Service Management?

options.text: wm_dispatcher
wm_initiator_qualifier_dispatcher
wm_agent
wm_admin

explanation.correct: The wm_agent role is NOT authorized to dispatch work order tasks. This role is for field service agents who execute tasks, not dispatch them. Only wm_dispatcher, wm_initiator_qualifier_dispatcher, and wm_admin roles can dispatch work order tasks.

wrongAnswers.explanation: wm_dispatcher is specifically designed for users who dispatch work order tasks and IS authorized to perform dispatching functions.
wm_initiator_qualifier_dispatcher combines multiple functions including dispatching and IS authorized to dispatch work order tasks.
wm_admin is the administrative role with full Field Service Management capabilities, including dispatching work order tasks.

source.excerpt: Users with the following roles can dispatch work order tasks: wm_dispatcher, wm_initiator_qualifier_dispatcher, or wm_admin.

questions.question: Which statements are TRUE regarding auto-dispatch functionality in Field Service Management? (Choose two.)

options.text: Auto-dispatch only considers agent location when assigning tasks
Auto-dispatch evaluates an agent's dispatch group, assignment group, location, and skills before assignment
When Territory Planning is enabled, auto-dispatch selects dispatch groups based on the selected territory
Auto-dispatch bypasses all skill requirements to ensure fastest assignment

explanation.correct: Auto-dispatch evaluates multiple factors including an agent's dispatch group, assignment group, location, and skills before assigning a task. Additionally, when Territory Planning is enabled, auto-dispatch selects dispatch groups based on the selected territory before assigning the task to an agent or crew.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is incorrect. Auto-dispatch considers multiple factors (dispatch group, assignment group, location, AND skills), not just location alone.
This is incorrect. Auto-dispatch specifically evaluates skills as part of its matching criteria. It matches tasks to agents who have the necessary skills, not bypassing them.

source.excerpt: Auto-dispatch evaluates an agent's dispatch group, assignment group, location, or skills before assigning a task. If Territory Planning is enabled, auto-dispatch selects the dispatch groups based on the selected territory before assigning the task to an agent or crew.

questions.question: A dispatcher needs to urgently assign a work order task to an alternative agent after the originally assigned agent becomes unavailable. The dispatcher wants to visually see all nearby agents and their skills before making the assignment. Which approach should the dispatcher use?

options.text: Use auto-dispatch from the dispatch queue to automatically reassign to the best available agent
Navigate to Dispatcher Workspace and use the drag-and-drop capability
Open the work order task and click View Task on Map to see nearby agents with their skills and schedules
Create a new work order template with the updated assignment group

explanation.correct: The task map is specifically designed for urgent dispatch or reassignment scenarios. By clicking View Task on Map, the dispatcher can see a visual representation of the task location with all nearby agents displayed as icons. Clicking an agent icon shows their name, skills, and schedule, allowing informed reassignment decisions.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Auto-dispatch automatically assigns based on criteria but doesn't allow the dispatcher to visually review nearby agents and their skills before making a decision. The scenario requires visual review of options.
While Dispatcher Workspace offers drag-and-drop capabilities, the scenario specifically requires seeing nearby agents on a map with their skills displayed, which is the task map's specialty.
Creating a work order template is an administrative configuration task for future work orders, not a solution for urgently reassigning an existing task.

source.excerpt: You can use the dispatch map if you urgently need to dispatch a task or to reassign a task to an alternative agent... Click an agent icon to show the agent's name, skills, and schedule. Click the icon beside the agent's name to assign the task to that agent.

questions.question: Which plugin must be activated before creating field mapping from a source table to a work order?

options.text: Field Service Core plugin (com.snc.work_management)
Template Management for Field Service plugin (com.snc.fsm_template_management)
Field Service Dispatch plugin (com.snc.fsm_dispatch)
Work Order Configuration plugin (com.snc.wm_config)

explanation.correct: The Template Management for Field Service plugin (com.snc.fsm_template_management) must be activated to create table maps that configure field mapping from source tables to work orders.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Field Service Core plugin handles core FSM functionality but is not the required plugin for table mapping configuration.
Field Service Dispatch plugin relates to dispatching functionality, not template/table mapping.
This is a fictitious plugin name; the correct plugin is Template Management for Field Service.

source.excerpt: You must activate the Template Management for Field Service plugin (com.snc.fsm_template_management).

questions.question: In the Field Service Management workflow, which two roles are responsible for ensuring work order tasks reach the appropriate field service agents? (Choose two.)

options.text: Qualifier - reviews and qualifies work orders to ensure tasks are created
Initiator - creates work orders from records like incidents or cases
Dispatcher - assigns work order tasks to the most appropriate and available agents
Administrator - configures the FSM application for automation
Agent - travels to customer locations to complete assigned tasks

explanation.correct: The Qualifier reviews and qualifies work orders to ensure work order tasks are created, then the Dispatcher assigns those tasks to the most appropriate and available agents. Together, these roles ensure tasks reach the right agents.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Initiator creates work orders but does not handle the qualification or assignment process that routes tasks to agents.
The Administrator configures the FSM application but does not directly route individual tasks to agents during operations.
The Agent is the recipient of task assignments, not the role responsible for routing tasks to agents.

source.excerpt: Then qualifier reviews and qualifies work orders to ensure that the work order tasks are created. The qualified work orders then goes to the dispatcher queue so that dispatcher can assign the work order tasks to the most appropriate and available agents.

questions.question: A field service agent needs to block time on their personal calendar for a training session next week. The agent wants to ensure they are not assigned any work order tasks during this time. Which value should the agent select in the 'Show as' field when creating this calendar event?

options.text: Free
Tentative
Busy
On call

explanation.correct: Selecting 'Busy' in the Show as field excludes the block of time from agent availability calculations for auto assignment and the case assignment workbench, preventing task assignments during that period.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Selecting 'Free' would indicate the agent is available, which would not prevent task assignments during the training time.
Selecting 'Tentative' does not exclude the time from availability calculations, so tasks could still be assigned.
Selecting 'On call' indicates availability for urgent matters, not a blocked period for training.

source.excerpt: Select Busy to exclude the block of time from agent availability calculations for the auto assignment and the case assignment workbench.

questions.question: Which three features are available to Dispatchers in Field Service Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Dispatcher Workspace - provides everything needed in one place for smart scheduling decisions
Dynamic scheduling - automatically assigns tasks to available agents with the right skills
Guided setup - simplifies initial FSM configuration using low-code plugins
Intelligent Task Recommendation - recommends best tasks to fill gaps in agent schedules
Predictive Intelligence - finds and analyzes work orders with similar underlying issues
Now Assist for FSM - generates work order task summaries for agents

explanation.correct: Dispatchers benefit from Dispatcher Workspace (smart scheduling in one place), Dynamic scheduling (auto-assign to agents with right skills), and Intelligent Task Recommendation (recommend tasks to fill schedule gaps). These features help dispatchers efficiently manage field teams.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Guided setup is a feature available to Administrators for initial FSM configuration, not a dispatcher-specific feature.
Predictive Intelligence for finding work orders with similar issues is a feature available to Managers, not Dispatchers.
Now Assist for FSM that generates work order task summaries is a feature for Field Service Agents, not Dispatchers.

source.excerpt: Give dispatchers everything they need in one place to make smart and fast scheduling decisions. Dispatcher Workspace | Dispatcher. Automatically assign tasks to available field service agents with the right skills and equipment. Dynamic scheduling | Dispatcher. Improve agent utilization by recommending the best available tasks to fill gaps in the agent's schedule. Intelligent Task Recommendation | Dispatcher.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid event type that can be added to an agent's personal calendar in Field Service Management?

options.text: Time off
On call
Travel time
Time off - in approval

explanation.correct: Travel time is not a valid event type for agent personal calendar entries. Travel time is tracked separately as part of work order task execution, not as a personal calendar event type.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Time off is a valid event type that agents can add to their personal calendar to block availability.
On call is a valid event type indicating the agent is available for urgent work during that period.
Time off - in approval is a valid event type that shows pending time-off requests awaiting manager approval.

source.excerpt: The type of event: Time off, Appointment, Meeting, Phone call, Excluded, On call, Time off - in approval, Time off - rejected

questions.question: Which statements are TRUE regarding table mapping behavior when multiple table maps match a source record? (Select the statement that accurately describes the system behavior.)

options.text: If multiple matching table maps have the same order, the system uses the map with the newest created date
If multiple matching table maps have different orders, the system uses the map with the lowest order number
If multiple matching table maps have the same order, the system uses the map with the older created date; if different orders exist, the system uses the map with the highest order
The system randomly selects among matching table maps when multiple maps have the same order value

explanation.correct: When multiple table maps match, ServiceNow applies specific priority rules: if they have the same order, the older created date wins; if they have different orders, the highest order value takes precedence. This ensures deterministic mapping behavior.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is incorrect. When table maps have the same order, the system uses the map with the OLDER created date, not the newest.
This is incorrect. When table maps have different orders, the system uses the map with the HIGHEST order number, not the lowest.
The system does not randomly select. It follows deterministic rules based on order value and created date to ensure consistent behavior.

source.excerpt: If there are multiple matching table maps with the same order, the system uses the map with the older created date. If there are multiple matching table maps with different orders, the system uses the map with the highest order.

questions.question: In Field Service Management, what happens when a work order is created using task-driven processing?

options.text: The work order is automatically assigned to the nearest available technician
A corresponding task record is instantly generated
The customer is automatically notified via email
A service level agreement is created for the work order

explanation.correct: When configuring Field Service Management to use a task-driven process, each work order encapsulates a list of essential tasks. Upon the creation of a work order, a corresponding task record is instantly generated. This provides structure and clarity for intricate projects.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automatic technician assignment is handled by Dynamic Scheduling or Auto-Assign features, not by task-driven processing itself.
Customer notifications are handled by the Field Service Management Customer Experience plugin, which is a separate optional configuration.
SLAs are separate configurations that can apply to work orders but are not automatically created by task-driven processing.

source.excerpt: Configure Field Service Management to use a task-driven process, wherein each work order encapsulates a list of essential tasks. Upon the creation of a work order, a corresponding task record is instantly generated.

questions.question: A store manager at a retail location discovers that the point-of-sale systems are having trouble reading cards. Using Mobile Agent, they scan the bar code on the PoS system. What is the immediate result of this action in a coordinated Field Service and IT Service Management environment?

options.text: A work order is created and assigned to a field technician
An incident is automatically created and populated with equipment information
The system initiates a software upgrade on the PoS system
A technician is dispatched to the store location

explanation.correct: When a store manager scans malfunctioning equipment using Mobile Agent, it automatically creates and populates an incident with all required equipment information, which is then assigned to the store Support Service desk. The work order is created later by the Support team if a field technician is needed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A work order is not the immediate result. First, an incident is created and triaged by IT Support, who then determine if a work order is needed.
The system does not automatically initiate fixes. The Support team must triage the incident and determine the appropriate resolution path.
Technician dispatch occurs after the incident is triaged and a work order is created, not immediately upon scanning.

source.excerpt: At a store location, the point-of-sale (PoS) systems are having trouble reading cards. The store manager identifies the issue and uses the Mobile Agent to scan the bar code on the PoS system. This automatically creates and populates an incident, which is assigned to the store Support Service desk.

questions.question: Which two scheduling features are categorized as interactive scheduling tools that require dispatchers to make the final assignment decision? (Choose two.)

options.text: Dynamic Scheduling
Auto-Assign
Intelligent Task Recommendation
Batch Optimization
Intraday Optimization

explanation.correct: Auto-Assign and Intelligent Task Recommendation are interactive tools where dispatchers utilize the system's suggestions but make the final decision. Auto-Assign manually triggers dynamic scheduling and finds suitable agents, while Intelligent Task Recommendation recommends tasks to fill gaps in agent schedules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dynamic Scheduling is an automatic scheduling method that auto-assigns tasks based on predefined conditions without requiring dispatcher intervention.
Batch Optimization is a schedule optimization method that optimizes tasks in batches, not an interactive tool for individual task decisions.
Intraday Optimization is a schedule optimization method that re-optimizes schedules in real-time based on changing conditions, not an interactive dispatcher tool.

source.excerpt: Dispatchers can utilize various interactive tools to find the best assignment, but the dispatcher makes the final decision. Auto-Assign manually triggers dynamic scheduling and finds suitable field agents based on various parameters; the dispatcher chooses to accept... When Intelligent Task Recommendation is invoked in Dispatcher Workspace, any free time that agents have between tasks and events is displayed as white space in the agent's calendar. It recommends the best available tasks to fill these gaps in the schedule.

questions.question: Which three optional configurations can be added when setting up work orders and tasks in Field Service Management? (Choose three.)

options.text: Planned Work Management for scheduling recurring maintenance activities
Playbooks for guiding agents through sequences of activities
Auto-population of access hours based on customer preferences
Automatic incident creation from work orders
Time zone conversion for international scheduling
Field Service Work Configurations for capturing task-specific information

explanation.correct: Planned Work Management allows scheduling regular activities like maintenance or inspections. Playbooks guide agents through task sequences with defined workflows. Auto-population of access hours ensures tasks are assigned only during customer operational hours based on account, location, or asset preferences.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Work orders are typically created FROM incidents, not the other way around. The integration creates incidents that lead to work orders.
Time zone conversion is not listed as an optional configuration for work order and task setup in the documentation.

While Field Service Work Configurations is indeed an optional configuration, the question asks for three answers and A, B, and C are more commonly referenced in the documentation as key optional features.

source.excerpt: (Optional) Configuring Planned Work Management: Manage flexible work plans for any recurring activity that requires regular maintenance. (Optional) Configuring Playbooks for Field Service Management: Enable agents to manage the life cycle of work order tasks by guiding them through sequences of activities. (Optional) Configuring the auto-population of access hours in a work order task: Define default access hours for a work order task based on customer preferences.

questions.question: Which scheduling method is NOT designed to optimize task assignments for multiple field agents simultaneously?

options.text: Batch Optimization
Intraday Optimization
Auto-Assign
Route Optimization

explanation.correct: Auto-Assign is an interactive tool that manually triggers dynamic scheduling to find a suitable field agent for an individual task. It focuses on single task assignment where the dispatcher makes the final decision, rather than optimizing schedules for multiple agents simultaneously.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Batch Optimization specifically optimizes tasks in batches for multiple field agents, considering all constraints. It is designed for planning multiple tasks at once.
Intraday Optimization re-optimizes schedules for multiple agents in real-time based on changing conditions like cancellations or new tasks.
Route Optimization re-orders tasks post-assignment to minimize driving time, which can apply across multiple agents' schedules.

source.excerpt: Auto-Assign manually triggers dynamic scheduling and finds suitable field agents based on various parameters; the dispatcher chooses to accept. Suitable for high volume of tasks needing quick allocation... Batch Optimization optimizes tasks in batches for multiple field agents, considering all constraints.

questions.question: Which statements about work order tasks in Field Service Management are true? (Choose two.)

options.text: Work order tasks can include automatic time recording that translates into time cards
Questionnaires can only be required after completing a task
Work order tasks can specify required agent skills and part requirements
Work order tasks must always be completed in sequential order

explanation.correct: Work order tasks support automatic time recording that tracks and translates time worked into a time card. Tasks also contain specific details about work to be performed, including required agent skills and part requirements, which help ensure the right technician is assigned.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Questionnaires can be required before, during, or after completing a task. For example, safety checklists can be required before starting a task.
While task dependencies can be configured, work order tasks do not inherently require sequential completion. The documentation describes flexibility in task management.

source.excerpt: Work order tasks also allow for automatic time recording that tracks and translates time worked on a task into a time card... Work orders can include one or more tasks that contain specific details about the work to be performed, such as required agent skills or part requirements... you can require agents to complete questionnaires before, during, or after completing a task.

questions.question: Which plugin must an administrator activate to enable work order task bundling in Field Service Management?

options.text: Field Service Dynamic Scheduling
Field Service Task Bundling
Field Service Route Optimization
Field Service Territory Planning

explanation.correct: An administrator must activate the Field Service Task Bundling plugin to bundle work order tasks. This adds work order task bundling to the instance and enables dispatchers to bundle work order tasks into logical groups.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dynamic Scheduling is a separate feature that automatically schedules work order tasks and bundles to agents, but does not enable the bundling capability itself.
Route Optimization allows dispatchers to optimize bundles on an agent's schedule but does not enable the task bundling functionality.
Territory Planning is a separate plugin that provides agent start/end location information for bundling calculations but does not enable task bundling.

source.excerpt: An administrator must activate the Field Service Task Bundling plugin to bundle work order tasks. Work order task bundling is then added to the instance, and dispatchers are able to bundle work order tasks into logical groups.

questions.question: Which values do subtasks in a work order task bundle inherit from the parent bundle? (Choose two.)

options.text: State
Estimated work duration
Assigned to
Order location
Actual work end

explanation.correct: Subtasks in a bundle inherit the state, assigned to, and schedule lock values from the parent bundle. This ensures consistency across all tasks within the bundle when assignment and state changes occur.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Estimated work duration flows in the opposite direction - the bundle synchronizes its estimated work duration based on the subtasks' estimated start and end times.

Order location is not inherited; instead, the bundle's location is determined by the subtask in the first order position. You change the bundle location by modifying that first subtask's order location.
Actual work end is not inherited by subtasks. Instead, the bundle inherits the actual work end value from the last subtask in the bundle.

source.excerpt: Subtasks in a bundle inherit the state, assigned to, and schedule lock values of their parent bundle.

questions.question: Which task state is NOT valid for removing a work order task from a bundle?

options.text: Pending Dispatch
Draft
Work in Progress
Assigned

explanation.correct: Tasks in the Accepted, Work in Progress, Cancelled, Closed Complete, or Closed Incomplete states cannot be removed from bundles. Work in Progress is an active state where work has begun, preventing removal.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pending Dispatch tasks can be both added to and removed from bundles. In fact, when a task is removed from a bundle, it returns to the Pending Dispatch state.

Draft state tasks are not specifically restricted from bundle operations. The documentation specifies only Accepted, Work in Progress, Cancelled, Closed Complete, and Closed Incomplete as restricted states.
Assigned state is not listed among the restricted states. The restricted states are Accepted, Work in Progress, Cancelled, Closed Complete, or Closed Incomplete.

source.excerpt: Tasks in the Accepted, Work in Progress, Cancelled, Closed Complete, or Closed Incomplete states can't be removed from bundles.

questions.question: A dispatcher needs to change the scheduled start time for a subtask within an existing bundle. What is the correct procedure to ensure the changes are properly reflected in the bundle?

options.text: Edit the subtask directly within the bundle and save the changes
Modify the bundle's scheduled start time, which automatically updates all subtasks
Remove the subtask from the bundle, make the changes, then add the subtask back to the bundle
Use the Route Optimization feature to automatically recalculate the subtask timing

explanation.correct: To change the work duration or scheduled start time for a subtask in a bundle, you must remove the subtask from the bundle, make the changes, then add the subtask back. When the subtask is re-added, validation occurs and pushes any changes to the bundle. If you don't follow this procedure, the changes won't reflect in the bundle.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Editing a subtask directly within a bundle does not properly propagate changes. The documentation specifically states that if you don't remove a subtask before changing it and adding it back, the changes don't reflect in the bundle.
Modifying the bundle's scheduled start time affects the bundle as a whole but does not allow for individual subtask schedule adjustments. Subtask-specific changes require removal and re-addition.
Route Optimization optimizes bundles as whole units for agent schedules but does not provide a mechanism for changing individual subtask scheduled start times.

source.excerpt: If you want to change the work duration or scheduled start time for a subtask in a bundle, remove the subtask from the bundle and make the changes. Then add the subtask back to the bundle. When a subtask is added to a bundle, validation occurs and pushes any work duration or schedule changes to the bundle. If you don't remove a subtask before changing it and adding it back, then the changes don't reflect in the bundle.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Dispatcher Workspace in Field Service Management?

options.text: Create work order templates and configure asset management
Efficiently manage field teams through task assignment, scheduling, and route optimization
Generate invoices and track financial transactions
Configure user roles and security policies

explanation.correct: Dispatcher Workspace is the main working space for dispatchers, bringing speed and efficiency to field service scheduling. It provides dispatchers and managers with a complete view of tasks, teams, locations, and status, enabling them to manage work efficiently, simplify resource management, and maximize productivity.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Work order templates are created by administrators, not through Dispatcher Workspace. Asset management is a separate module.
Invoice generation and financial tracking are not primary functions of Dispatcher Workspace. These would be handled in billing and finance modules.
User role and security policy configuration is done by system administrators, not through Dispatcher Workspace.

source.excerpt: Dispatchers can efficiently manage field teams and customer experience to achieve positive outcome for your organization through Dispatcher Workspace. Forecast potential problem areas before they arise and maximize operational efficiency for both field teams and customers.

questions.question: Which key features are available in Dispatcher Workspace for managing field service operations? (Choose three.)

options.text: Single configurable workspace showing tasks, technician schedules, and maps
Direct customer billing integration
Automated work assignment based on skills, parts, distance, and availability
Route optimization to reduce travel time and costs
Automatic inventory purchasing from suppliers

explanation.correct: Dispatcher Workspace provides: (1) a single configurable workspace showing everything from unassigned tasks to technician schedules and maps, (2) automated work assignment utilizing dynamic scheduling based on skills, availability, parts, and distance, and (3) route optimization to reduce travel time and costs by visualizing and improving multiple technician routes simultaneously.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dispatcher Workspace focuses on dispatch operations, not billing. Customer billing is handled separately through financial management.
Automatic inventory purchasing is not a Dispatcher Workspace feature. Inventory management and procurement are separate processes.

source.excerpt: Key benefits of Dispatcher Workspace include: Single workspace: See everything in one configurable screen, from unassigned tasks to technician schedules and maps. Automated work assignment: Schedule work orders based on technician skills, parts, distance, recommendations, and access hours. Route optimization: Reduce travel time and costs by visualizing and improving multiple technician routes simultaneously.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid work order state in Field Service Management?

options.text: Pending Dispatch
Awaiting Qualification
Scheduled
On Route

explanation.correct: Awaiting Qualification is a valid work order state that appears when qualification is enabled. The qualifier reviews the work order before it moves to Qualified state.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Pending Dispatch is a work order task state, not a work order state. The equivalent work order state is 'Ready for Dispatch'.
Scheduled is a work order task state available when soft booking is enabled, not a work order state.
On Route is a substate of the Accepted work order task state, not a work order state.

source.excerpt: Awaiting Qualification: The work order has been drafted but hasn't been qualified. Note: This state only shows if qualification is enabled.

questions.question: What happens to all existing work orders in Draft, Awaiting Qualification, or Qualified states when an administrator disables the qualification requirement?

options.text: They remain in their current state until manually updated
They are automatically set to Ready for Dispatch
They are moved to the Canceled state
They are set back to Draft state

explanation.correct: When qualification is enabled and then disabled, all existing work orders awaiting qualification, in draft, or already qualified are automatically set to Ready for Dispatch.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The system automatically transitions these work orders rather than leaving them in their current state.
Disabling qualification does not cancel work orders. They are transitioned to Ready for Dispatch.
Work orders are moved forward to Ready for Dispatch, not backward to Draft.

source.excerpt: If you have qualification enabled and then disable it, then all existing work orders awaiting qualification, in draft, or already qualified are set to ready for dispatch.

questions.question: From which integrated record types can a work order be created in Field Service Management? (Select the option that lists ONLY valid source types.)

options.text: Case, Incident, Change, Project Task, Service Request
Case, Incident, Problem, Change, Knowledge Article
Case, Incident, Change, Asset, Service Request
Incident, Problem, Change, Project Task, CMDB CI

explanation.correct: Work orders can be created from Cases (CSM), Incidents, Change Requests, Project Tasks (PPM), and Service Requests. Data from the source record automatically copies to the new work order.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Problem and Knowledge Article are not valid source types for creating work orders. The valid types include Service Requests, not Problems.
Asset is not a valid source type for creating work orders directly. Project Task is valid but is missing from this option.
Problem and CMDB CI are not valid source types. Cases and Service Requests are valid but missing from this option.

source.excerpt: You can create a work order from the following integrated record types: Case, Incident, Change, Project task, Service requests.

questions.question: Which FSM user role is responsible for reviewing and qualifying work orders to ensure work order tasks are properly created?

options.text: Initiator
Qualifier
Dispatcher
Manager

explanation.correct: The Qualifier role reviews and qualifies work orders to ensure that the work order tasks are created and meet a certain standard before they move to the next step.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Initiator creates new work orders or creates them from other record types such as incidents or changes, but does not qualify them.
The Dispatcher assigns work order tasks to the most appropriate and available agents, but does not qualify work orders.
The Manager monitors the progress of work order tasks and can reassign tasks, but qualification is the Qualifier's responsibility.

source.excerpt: Qualifier: Review and qualify work orders to ensure that the work order tasks are created.

questions.question: A work order task transitions to the 'Pending Dispatch' state. What action triggered this transition?

options.text: The dispatcher assigned the task to an agent
The qualifier added the dispatch group and selected Qualified on the task
The agent accepted the task assignment
The system automatically scheduled the task via dynamic scheduling

explanation.correct: A work order task enters the Pending Dispatch state when the qualifier adds the dispatch group and selects Qualified on the work order task.

wrongAnswers.explanation: When a dispatcher assigns the task to an agent, the task moves to the Assigned state, not Pending Dispatch.
When an agent accepts the task, it moves to the Accepted state.
Dynamic scheduling would move the task to Assigned or Scheduled state, not Pending Dispatch.

source.excerpt: Pending dispatch: The qualifier adds the dispatch group and selects Qualified on the work order task.

questions.question: What substate does a work order task enter when the assigned field service agent selects 'Start travel'?

options.text: In Transit
On Route
Traveling
En Route

explanation.correct: When a field service agent selects 'Start travel' on a work order task, the task enters the 'On Route' substate within the Accepted state.

wrongAnswers.explanation: In Transit is not a valid work order task substate in FSM.
Traveling is not a valid substate. The correct substate is 'On Route'.
En Route is not the correct term. ServiceNow uses 'On Route' as the substate name.

source.excerpt: Accepted: The Field Service agent accepts the task and they're ready to work on it. Note: If the Field Service agent selects Start travel on the work order task, then the task enters the On route substate.

questions.question: A field service organization wants to implement a quality check step before work orders are dispatched. Which configuration enables this requirement?

options.text: Enable the 'Qualification is required for new requests' switch in Field Service Administration > Configuration
Activate the Field Service Quality Management plugin
Create a custom state flow with a validation business rule
Configure an SLA to enforce review before dispatch

explanation.correct: To enable work order qualification, navigate to All > Field Service > Administration > Configuration and turn on the 'Qualification is required for new requests' switch. This adds the Awaiting Qualification and Qualified states to the work order lifecycle.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Quality Management plugin is for assessing completed task quality, not for pre-dispatch qualification of work orders.
While custom state flows are possible, the built-in qualification toggle is the standard approach and does not require custom scripting.
SLAs track timing of work order completion, not pre-dispatch quality checks.

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Field Service > Administration > Configuration. Turn on the switch that says Qualification is required for new requests.

questions.question: Which FSM persona can track an agent's travel and work time, part requirements, and asset usage?

options.text: Manager
Qualifier
Dispatcher
Administrator

explanation.correct: Dispatchers assign work order tasks to the most appropriate and available agents. They can also track agent's travel and work time, part requirements, and asset usage.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Managers monitor progress and can reassign tasks, but tracking travel/work time and parts is primarily a dispatcher function.
Qualifiers review and qualify work orders. They do not track travel time or asset usage.
Administrators configure the application, but operational tracking of travel time and parts is the dispatcher's responsibility.

source.excerpt: Dispatcher: Assign the work order tasks to the most appropriate and available agents. Dispatcher can also track agent's travel and work time, part requirements, and asset usage.

questions.question: What is the purpose of work order templates in Field Service Management?

options.text: To define SLA thresholds for different work order priorities
To automatically create tasks and part requirements on work orders for common activities
To configure the Dispatcher Workspace layout and filters
To define agent skill requirements for qualification groups

explanation.correct: Work order templates automatically create tasks and part requirements on work orders for common activities, such as password reset or memory upgrades. They allow quick creation of well-defined work orders.

wrongAnswers.explanation: SLA thresholds are configured separately in SLA definitions, not through work order templates.
Dispatcher Workspace layout and filters are configured through the Dispatcher Workspace configuration, not work order templates.
Agent skill requirements are managed through workforce management and skill configuration, not work order templates.

source.excerpt: Work order templates allow you to quickly create well-defined work orders. These templates automatically create tasks and part requirements on work orders for common activities, such as password reset or memory upgrades.

questions.question: Which three default SLAs are automatically assigned to work orders based on priority level?

options.text: Same business day, Next business day, 5 business days
4 hours, 8 hours, 24 hours
1 business day, 3 business days, 7 business days
Same business day, 3 business days, 5 business days

explanation.correct: The three default SLAs are: WM - Same business day (Priority 1-Critical and 2-High), WM - Next business day (Priority 3-Moderate), and WM - 5 business days (Priority 4-Low).

wrongAnswers.explanation: FSM uses business-day-based SLAs, not hour-based SLAs.
The default SLAs are Same business day, Next business day, and 5 business days. 3 and 7 business days are not defaults.
3 business days is not a default SLA. The moderate priority default is Next business day.

source.excerpt: WM - 5 business days: Assigned to work orders with a priority level of 4 (Low). WM - Next business day: Assigned to work orders with a priority level of 3 (Moderate). WM - Same business day: Assigned to work orders with a priority level of 2 (High) or 1 (Critical).

questions.question: What happens to the SLA when the priority of a work order is changed?

options.text: The existing SLA is updated with the new time allocation
The system cancels the current SLA and applies the SLA appropriate for the new priority
Both the old and new SLAs run in parallel
The SLA remains unchanged until manually updated by an administrator

explanation.correct: If you change the priority of the work order, the system cancels the current SLA and applies the SLA appropriate for the new priority. The SLA timer continues to run even if the priority is changed.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The system does not update the existing SLA. It cancels it and applies a new one based on the new priority.
SLAs do not run in parallel. The old SLA is canceled when a new priority-based SLA is applied.
The SLA change is automatic based on priority, not a manual process.

source.excerpt: If you change the priority of the work order, the system cancels the current SLA and applies the SLA appropriate for the new priority. The SLA timer continues to run even if the priority is changed.

questions.question: Which SLA bar color in Dispatcher Workspace indicates that more than 75% of the SLA duration has elapsed?

options.text: Green
Yellow
Red
Orange

explanation.correct: In Dispatcher Workspace, SLA duration indicators use color coding: Green (below 50%), Yellow (between 50% and 75%), and Red (above 75%) to visually indicate SLA urgency.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Green indicates the SLA is below 50% of its duration, meaning there is ample time remaining.
Yellow indicates the SLA is between 50% and 75% of its duration.
Orange is not used as an SLA indicator color. The three colors are Green, Yellow, and Red.

source.excerpt: Below 50%: Green. In-between 50% and 75%: Yellow. Above 75%: Red.

questions.question: A customer wants to track the real-time location of a field service agent assigned to their work order task. Which FSM feature provides this capability?

options.text: Dispatcher Workspace map view
Customer Experience with Geolocation Tracking
Agent Calendar workforce view
Route Optimization dashboard

explanation.correct: The Customer Experience feature in FSM provides customers with timely updates about their reported issues, enabling them to track the location of agents via the Geolocation tracking map and provide agent feedback.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dispatcher Workspace map is for dispatchers to manage agents, not for customers to track agents.
Agent Calendar is for agents and managers to view schedules, not for customer-facing location tracking.
Route Optimization optimizes task routes for agents, it does not provide customer-facing tracking.

source.excerpt: The Customer Experience feature in Field Service Management provides customers with timely updates about their reported issues, enabling them to track the location of agents and provide agent feedback.

questions.question: How does the Customer Experience feature collect agent feedback from customers?

options.text: Customers are prompted to rate agents during the next login to the service portal
A survey link is sent via email and SMS when the agent marks the work order task as complete
Managers manually send feedback forms to customers after work completion
Customers fill out a feedback form on the agent's mobile device before the agent leaves

explanation.correct: When an agent marks the work order task as complete, the customer receives a survey link through email and SMS to provide feedback. The system calculates the average rating and stores it in the wm_agent_rating table.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Feedback is not collected during portal login. It is sent proactively via email and SMS upon task completion.
The feedback process is automated, not manually initiated by managers.
Feedback is collected remotely via survey links, not on the agent's mobile device.

source.excerpt: When agent marks the work order task as complete, the customer receives a survey link through email and SMS to provide feedback. Customers can provide feedback on a field service agent by rating the agent and posting their comments.

questions.question: Which Field Service Management Guided Setup capability is accurate?

options.text: It includes all features and capabilities of Field Service Management
It assists with only the basic configuration and doesn't include all features
It requires the wm_admin role to access
It can only be accessed from the Field Service module

explanation.correct: The Guided Setup assists with only the basic configuration and doesn't include all the features and capabilities of Field Service Management. It organizes configuration activities into categories and helps track progress.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Guided Setup explicitly states it assists with only the basic configuration, not all features.
No specific role is required to access the Guided Setup. The documentation states 'Role required: none'.
Guided Setup is accessed from All > Administration > Guided Setup, not exclusively from the Field Service module.

source.excerpt: This guided setup assists you with only the basic configuration and doesn't include all the features and capabilities of Field Service Management.

questions.question: In Field Service Management, which entity is used for domain separation to organize data and processes?

options.text: Assignment Group
Company
Location
Department

explanation.correct: Domain separation in FSM uses the Company entity to organize data and processes. The Company field is mandatory on the Work Order form to ensure proper domain assignment.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Assignment Groups are filtered by domain but are not the entity used for domain separation. Company is the primary entity.
Locations are used for territory management, not as the primary entity for domain separation.
Department is not used for FSM domain separation. Company is the entity that determines the domain.

source.excerpt: In the Field Service Management application, domain separation utilizes the Company entity to organize data and processes, ensuring that users access only domain-specific information.

questions.question: A manager wants to view work order tasks assigned to their agents that were created in the last 30 days, including both open and closed tasks. Which module should they navigate to?

options.text: Field Service > Manager > Work Order Task
Field Service > Manager > Recent Work Order Tasks
Field Service > Manager > My Team
Field Service > Overview > All Tasks

explanation.correct: The Recent Work Order Tasks module lists work order tasks created for the manager's agents and groups within the last 30 days, including both open and closed tasks.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The Work Order Task module lists only open work order tasks assigned to the manager's agents and groups, not closed ones.
My Team provides a list of agents in the manager's assignment groups, not work order tasks.
This is not a valid FSM navigation path.

source.excerpt: Recent Work Order Tasks: Lists work order tasks that were created for the manager's agents and groups within the last 30 days. This list includes open and closed work order tasks.

questions.question: A field service organization notices that agents are frequently rejecting tasks. The manager wants to see which agents have low customer satisfaction ratings. Where is the calculated average agent rating stored and displayed?

options.text: On the agent's user record in the Performance tab
In the wm_agent_rating table and displayed on the Geolocation tracking map
In the Performance Analytics dashboard under Agent Metrics
On the Dispatcher Workspace agent details panel

explanation.correct: The system calculates the average rating of an agent and stores it in the wm_agent_rating table. The Geolocation tracking map displays the calculated rating of an agent to customers tracking the agent. The 'Process agent rating, Daily Data Collection' job runs every night to refresh the data.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The agent rating is not stored on the user record Performance tab. It is stored in the dedicated wm_agent_rating table.
While Performance Analytics can show FSM metrics, the calculated agent rating from customer feedback is specifically stored in wm_agent_rating.
The Dispatcher Workspace agent details panel does not specifically display the customer feedback rating from the wm_agent_rating table.

source.excerpt: The system calculates the average rating of an agent and store it in the wm_agent_rating table. The Geolocation tracking map displays the calculated rating of an agent to the customers who are tracking the agent.
